notes: A clean three-NM chain and one of the better evidence ladders in this batch: each NM's drop is consumed by the next trade, so Darksteel Ingot, Gerwitz's Axe and Gerwitz's Sword can each be evidence exactly once without any of them being live on two rungs at the same time. Bullets 6 and 9 are pure in-zone routing -- south up the ramp, down the southeast hole at (H-11/12) to map 3, then south into the square room -- and are folded into the trades they lead to rather than given rungs of their own; nothing about walking across Ordelle's Caves is markable or observable. Bullet 11 is two different things and is split: killing Gerwitz's Soul, then zoning out to La Theine Plateau at (G-10), which is where the cutscene and the reward actually happen. That means the quest ends on a zone line with no hand-in NPC, so no turn-in is invented. The unnumbered line under bullet 1 ('You can be on any job from here on') is a comment on the Dark Knight gate, not a step. FLevel is 'NA', so the fame level is null while the region stands.

notes:
Two targets in this quest have no name on the page and neither is guessed at. Bullet 2 says only 'the pools' -- three little green marks on map 2 of Fei'Yin -- and bullet 7 says only 'a chest'; writing ??? or Treasure Chest for either would be inventing a name, so both steps keep their rung and their zone and lose their marker honestly. A human with the client open could recover both cheaply, which is why they are flagged. The three pools are ONE step rather than three: they are examined in a fixed order ((H-8), (H-5), then lastly (F-5)) and nothing about the first two is observable, so three rungs the player cannot be tracked through would be noise. Step 1's evidence is also lost, for a different reason: the page says Brutus grants three Aquaflora key items, but 'Aquaflora' is not a unique name in the client's key-item table and the resolver rejects it rather than guess an id, so the step is left evidence-free instead of carrying a wrong one. Bullet 3 contradicts itself -- the ghost 'can actually spawn at any pool' but seems to need the other two used first -- and the walkthrough's stated order is what is recorded. The Castle Oztroja half carries itself on the Oztroja Chest Key and the Beast Collar; the Curio Vendor Moogle alternative needs no branch, because the evidence is the key however you came by it.

Bullet 1's rule that no other Weapon Skill quest may be active is an entry gate with no schema slot and nothing observable; Quest Reqs' 'Dagger skill 230+' is a second gate with no slot; and the 'Breaking the Latent' sub-bullet arrived as a bare transcluded heading with its content missing, so a genuine requirement sitting between rungs 1 and 2 is on the page in name only. The rest of that note -- it cannot be started while this quest or Making the Grade is active -- has no schema slot and is not a step. Bullet 1 is two NPCs and becomes two rungs, Mashuu-Ajuu first and then Paku-Nakku, in the order the page insists on; start stays on the header's Paku-Nakku because he is the giver and both stand at (K-6), so nothing moves on the map either way. notes:
Only bullets 1 and 2 are the quest. Bullet 3 is Home Point advice, bullet 4 is an outcome (she removes the ailment as she pays you), and the 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section is trivia about the Japanese title -- none of them is a step. Bullet 2 is the whole substance of the quest and it is a five-way OR across five zones: Bane from Lost Souls in The Eldieme Necropolis, Mute from Eight of Cups in the Outer Horutoto Ruins entered at (F-11) in West Sarutabaruta, and Plague from Bloodsuckers in Toraimarai Canal, Deathmaw Orobons in Ceizak Battlegrounds or Devouring Mosquitoes in Reisenjima. The zone changes per branch so the step records none, exactly as a per-battle-zone step would. The five monsters are deliberately NOT in mobs[]: you do not have to kill any of them, you have to be hit by one, and none of kill/drop/spawn says that -- listing them would place markers on an assertion the page does not make. Nor is any of it observable: a status effect is not an item or a key item, so the middle step carries no evidence and the ladder crosses it on the session latch. Everything a player actually needs is in that step's note. Quest Reqs is the status effect itself restated, so it gates nothing, and the reward varies by which ailment you brought.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 2: Five branches in five zones, so no zone is recorded; being hit by a monster is not a role the schema has, so none of them is listed as a mob.

notes: The same Resistance Sapper and the same once-per-Vana'dielian-day cooldown as Desert Rain I, shared across every Abyssea area and invisible to the addon. This one models better than its sibling because both of its key items are real: the fluid on the way out and the bottle on the way back. The Rear Trap is clicked twice -- once to prime it and be told the distance to stand at, and once more from that distance to run the infusion -- and both are kept as rungs, because they sit on the same markable object and cost nothing, while the second is where the evidence lands. The page says outright that the Paralysis trap fluid bottle arrives with 'no indication', which is precisely the case for evidence rather than against it: the packet carries the key item even though the player is never told. The 1 / 2 / 5 yalm choice only scales the reward, so it is a note and not a branch, and bullet 2's travel folds into the click it leads to. Fame 'amis' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so the region is null and raw is kept.

notes:
Bullet 2 is the one awkward step on the page: 'head to any Telepoint and trade a synthesis crystal'. The Telepoint is named and markable, but there are three of them in three different zones, so the step carries a null zone rather than picking one -- a nil-zone row matches everywhere, which is the honest answer for 'any'. What you trade is 'a synthesis crystal', a category of eight items the page never names one of, so items is empty and items_partial records that the requirement could not be expressed at all rather than pretending there is no requirement. The Faded Crystal it yields is the header's Item Req and is obtained here rather than rewarded, so it is legitimate evidence for that step, and it is consumed at step 3, so it is evidence only once. Bullets 3, 4 and 5 are one trade -- travel to Xarcabard, find the ??? in the glowing trenches at (E-8), trade the crystal -- because the travel and the search have the same zone and the same grid as the thing you finally click. Bullet 6 is split: the kill that drops the Glowstone, then the return to Chumimi, who takes it. 'Repeatable: af' is the artifact-armour category leaking into that field and means false. Which of the three magi you agree with in the opening cutscene decides only your title, so it is not a branch.
